name: SMT101x Sensors
description: Two modes for SMT101x tablets: recover the OEM publisher using your existing external MQTT settings, or manage sensors, switches, doors, and RGB backlight through Kiosk Satellite using the built-in local broker, with no separate MQTT server required.
author: Stuart Pearson

settings.title: Automatically re-enable disabled tablet MQTT
settings.description: Turn the tablet's MQTT switch back on if it has been disabled. Requires automatic recovery and works with either a local or external MQTT server. Leave off if you want to be able to turn MQTT off yourself. Your server address and login details are kept unchanged. Turning MQTT on does not guarantee that readings are reaching their destination.

settings.title: Automatically recover stopped OEM MQTT publisher
settings.description: Restart the tablet's built-in MQTT service if it stops, so readings can resume. Works in either mode on supported firmware. Checks once a minute and waits five minutes between recovery attempts. Does not fix Wi-Fi, server problems, or a service that is running but disconnected. Leaves MQTT switched off unless automatic re-enabling is also enabled.

settings.title: Host MQTT capture broker on this tablet
settings.description: Turn on to use the tablet's sensors and controls in Kiosk Satellite without a separate MQTT server. In Android's MQTT settings, set the server to 127.0.0.1 and port to 1883. Turn off to keep using your own MQTT server; automatic recovery can still be used, but no local entities are created. This option does not change Android's MQTT settings for you.

settings.title: MQTT client ID (optional)
settings.description: Usually leave this blank: the plugin learns the tablet's ID automatically when it sends status updates. If you enter an ID, copy the client_id value from Android's MQTT settings exactly, for example office. Used for local sensor management; it does not change the tablet's ID.
